blocks.task_summary: Find the predicted population at the start of 2026 given the rate of change dP/dt = 104000 e^{-0.0145t} and initial population 6.78 × 10^6 at t=0 (start of 2022).
method_path: Set up integral of rate of change from t=0 to t=4
Evaluate definite integral to find change in population
Add initial population to change to get final population
accepted_alternatives: Use indefinite integral to find general solution P(t) = -7172413.7... e^{-0.0145t} + c, determine c using initial condition, then evaluate at t=4.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: attempt to find change in population using a definite integral (M1); t=4 at the start of 2026 (A1); ∫_0^4 104000 e^{-0.0145t} dt (A1); = -404165.8... (A1); attempt to add initial population to their change (M1); population = 6.78×10^6 - 404165.8... = 6375834.1... ≈ 6.38×10^6 (A1). METHOD 2: indefinite integral approach with same final answer.
